The medical term for putting an animal to sleep is euthanasia, which is derived from a compound Greek word that literally translates to “good death.”1 It describes the practice of humanely and peacefully ending the life of an animal through medical means.1 It’s often referred to euphemistically as “putting to sleep” because the animal is fully sedated and falls asleep prior to stopping their heart, ensuring that they feel no pain. Is your kitty sufficiently hydrated, either through consuming liquids or subcutaneous fluids? - Hygiene. Is your kitty able to groom themselves and keep themselves clean? If someone has not personally experienced a loss of this magnitude, they won’t be able to relate to a pet parent who is grieving. Here’s how it works: - Sedation – Most veterinarians, during the dog check up will administer a sedative to help your dog relax and enjoy deep sleep before the final shot. - Euthanasia Injection – Once your dog is fully asleep, a second injection is given, usually containing pentobarbital, a medication that quickly and painlessly stops the heart. - Final Moments – Within a few seconds to a couple of minutes, your dog will pass peacefully, without pain or distress. Knowing that the process is gentle and designed to minimize suffering can help provide some comfort during this difficult time. How Much Does It Cost to Euthanize a Dog?
